chapter: Erroll Garner and the Los Angeles scene
title: Jack's Basket and the Los Angeles jam scene
summary: Jack's was the main jam spot with Wardell and Dexter dueling.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: While we're here, I'd like to ask you what else you remember about that California jamming scene.
The jamming scene? What's this?
When you were in L.A., you know, with Bird and Tatum and Dexter Gordon and Wardell Gray and all these people...

Oh yeah. Well, the main place where most of the musicians would hang out in California was Jack's. Like, all the saxophone players, Wardell and Dexter and Teddy Edwards and so forth, would hang out down there. But they had Art Tatum up at Lovejoy's, and somebody else used to go hang up there, too... Besides Garner. I mean...
What about Nat King Cole? He was around there, too, wasn't he, at different times?

Yeah. But he didn't come out and jam too much, because he was... You know, he was a big money man. He couldn't afford to be seen out in them after-hour joints and so forth. So he was making his money the other way. But as far as I can tell you about the sessions, the greatest sessions that I heard out there were at Jack's. You know, there were a lot of saxophone players that used to play there, and I'd go and jam sometimes with them.
Jack's Basket, I think it was called.
Yeah.
I've heard of that.
McGhee (12/6) - 61

That was the joint where the real heavy swing Jazz was being played. You know, Wardell and Dexter used to tie up every night practically. And Wardell was playing, too, man. He was playing some horn, man. But Dexter was in there, too. He was fighting right there with him.

I don't think Illinois got into that, you know. When he was out there, he stayed by himself. But I mean, we liked for him to come on and socialize with the guys, but I mean, like he felt funny about that or something, or he didn't believe in doing that. But we missed him. You know, we wanted him. We'd tell him, 'Come on, Jacquet, let's...' He got a certain thing off of the (?), too. I mean, I think he plays magnificent.
He sure does.

And he's got something to say, so we might as well listen to him too. But I mean, sometimes it don't happen that way, you know. I've seen him come out when he would bring his horn, you know, but... I mean, Dexter and Wardell was fighting it out anyway, so I guess he figured he wasn't needed. But we liked him anyway.
So now, who else do you want to talk about?
Well, I was just interested in that whole period, because there was so much jamming going on both after hours
McGhee (12/6) - 62
Yeah, the concerts was the thing, because...
I mean, it started with Jazz At The Philharmonic, and then it caught on with all the other... Just Jazz.
Gene Norman's affairs. Somebody else... Bass, Ralph Bass had his thing going, with his Jazz concerts. But overall, that was about it.
